extracted.intended_audience: researchers, prospective arXiv authors, and general readers interested in arXiv's submission and moderation practices
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for preparing and submitting e-prints to the arXiv repository, including moderation/endorsement rules, allowed formats, metadata/licensing options, and withdrawal policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation process
rubrics_metrics.description: A collection of moderators for each area review submissions; they may recategorize any that are deemed off-topic, or reject submissions that are not scientific papers, or sometimes for undisclosed reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderators operate per subject area; lists of moderators for many sections are publicly available (though many physics moderators remain unlisted). Moderators can reclassify submissions (e.g., move dubious work to 'General mathematics' rather than delete). The moderation process has attracted criticism for lack of transparency and for potentially restricting content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated quality control
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to human moderators, all submissions are checked via an automated quality control process, ensuring a baseline standard of professionalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automated checks enforce technical/professional baseline standards (complementing human moderation). Failures in these checks can lead to rejection (see technical rejection criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Endorsement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'endorsement' system requires, for categories that use it, that an author be endorsed by an established arXiv author before being allowed to submit papers to those categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endorsers are asked to check whether the paper is appropriate for the intended subject area, not to review the paper for errors. New authors from recognized academic institutions generally receive automatic endorsement. The endorsement system has been criticized for allegedly restricting scientific inquiry and creating a barrier for some authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted content types (policy for review/position papers and conference material)
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv is not peer reviewed; it has explicit policies on what content types are accepted: it announced (Nov 2025) that it would no longer accept computer science review articles and position papers that had not been vetted by an academic journal or conference, and it does not accept articles from conference workshops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review articles and position papers in affected categories should be accepted by a peer-reviewed journal or conference with reference and DOI metadata before submission. Conference workshop articles are rejected because they 'do not meet the same standard of rigor of traditional peer review.' arXiv states some source types 'were never officially on arXiv’s list of “accepted content types”.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical submission and rejection rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers can be submitted in several formats (including LaTeX and PDF printed from a word processor); the submission is rejected by the arXiv software if generating the final PDF file fails, if any image file is too large, or if the total size of the submission is too large.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: arXiv allows one to store/modify an incomplete submission and finalize it when ready; the time stamp is set when the submission is finalized. Authors should ensure successful PDF generation, keep image sizes within limits, and keep the total submission size within allowed bounds to avoid automatic rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifier, versioning, and category tagging
rubrics_metrics.description: Each arXiv paper has a uniquely specific identifier (YYMM.NNNNN or legacy archive/YYMMNNN) and different versions are specified by a version number at the end (e.g., 1709.08980v1). Each paper is tagged with one or more categories; some categories have two layers (e.g., q-fin.TR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no version number is specified, the default is the latest version. Properly choose categories/subcategories to reflect the paper's subject; moderators may recategorize off-topic submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal and retraction reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Preprints have been withdrawn (reported ~14,000) most commonly due to 'crucial errors'; a lesser number were withdrawn because the preprint was subsumed by another publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and readers should understand withdrawal is used primarily for critical errors or duplication/subsumption; arXiv's withdrawal statistics and reports are posted (e.g., a December 2024 report).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and licensing options
rubrics_metrics.description: Files on arXiv can have various copyright statuses: public domain; Creative Commons licenses (CC BY-SA 4.0 or CC BY-NC-SA 4.0); copyright to a publisher with the author having the right to distribute; or most commonly copyright to the author with arXiv holding a non-exclusive irrevocable license to distribute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must indicate the correct copyright/licensing status when submitting. arXiv's license information is publicly documented and determines how works may be redistributed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metadata availability and indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata for arXiv is made available through OAI-PMH (the standard for open access repositories) and is indexed by major consumers like BASE, CORE, and Unpaywall; arXiv is a top host of green open access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers can use metadata via OAI-PMH for harvesting; users can subscribe to sub-field daily emailings or RSS feeds of submissions. Proper metadata (including DOI when applicable) improves discoverability and compliance with arXiv policies for certain content types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderator transparency and public lists
rubrics_metrics.description: The lists of moderators for many sections of arXiv are publicly available, but moderators for most of the physics sections remain unlisted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public moderator lists improve transparency; lack of listing in some sections has been a point of contention. Awareness of who moderates a section may help authors understand subject-area norms and potential recategorization behavior.
